stories.headline: Bitcoin slides back to the $83k range floor as a long flush hits
stories.blurb: After a third rejection near $87k, BTC dropped to an intraday low around $82.8k on Oct 7; roughly half a billion dollars of mostly long positions were liquidated. — The ~$83k floor of the post-Sept-21 range is now the line; analysts flag buy orders near $81k, and losing that opens room toward the high-$70ks.

stories.headline: Oil tops $101 on Hormuz tanker attacks, pushing yields and the dollar up
stories.blurb: Brent climbed above $101, the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest since 2002 and the dollar index touched its highest since March 2025. — The energy-driven drop in yields that helped BTC rally in late September has reversed — macro is a headwind again.

stories.headline: Fed minutes: most officials see another hike by year-end, no rush for October
stories.blurb: Minutes of the Sept 15–16 meeting show a unanimous hike and most participants expecting one more increase by year-end, with timing left to the data. — Rate path stays restrictive; September CPI on Oct 14 and the Oct 27–28 FOMC are the next swing events for crypto's range.

stories.headline: Bitcoin ETFs back to inflows on IBIT while ether funds bleed for a sixth day
stories.blurb: Spot BTC ETFs took in about $119M on Oct 6, almost all via BlackRock's IBIT; ether ETFs lost about $202M, a sixth straight outflow. — Institutional demand is narrowing to BTC — a soft spot for altcoins, which matters for a SOL-heavy model.

stories.headline: Glassnode: the rally leaned on derivatives, with thin spot volume
stories.blurb: Glassnode found the late-September advance rested more on derivatives bets than new buyers, with spot volume among the thinnest since early 2024. — Leverage-led moves unwind fast; until spot demand returns, rallies into $87k stay fragile and dips can cascade.
